description: P1 retirement scrub (FR-013). The CI test-selection basis (dorny filter groups + --cov targets) re-derived against the LIVE post-#3921 src/** tree. The WP02 census oracle (tests/architectural/_p1_census_oracle.py) is the authority: no kept group maps a filter group or a --cov target onto a retired subsystem (sync/saas/delivery/event_journal/egress/websockets) or any census-dead surface, and every excluded surface cites the oracle's independent evidence. This is the single data source WP07 (router groups) and WP08 (module registry / shard-freeze) consume -- they derive from it, they do not re-scrub. It lands BEFORE the --durations shard-freeze so shard boundaries are measured on the scrubbed live basis. Enforced by tests/architectural/test_retirement_scrub.py.
notes: Coverage form (C-005): --cov targets are kept in dotted module form (never path form) and pyproject [tool.coverage.run].relative_files=true is preserved -- both are required for multi-<source> coverage resolution by the downstream aggregators.

Re-derivation (moves, NOT census exclusions): the historical standalone 'doctrine' group (src/doctrine/**) and the --cov=doctrine.missions target were re-mapped to their live successor src/charter/offering/** (doctrine absorbed into charter/offering post-convergence); doctrine is a MOVE, not a retirement, so it is not in excluded_surfaces. The stale core_misc root src/specify_cli/render/** was dropped -- the render package no longer exists (oracle: importer-count:0), so it is not carried by any kept group.

The enforcement allowlists (test_no_dead_symbols / test_no_dead_modules / test_no_retired_subsystems) that QUOTE dead surfaces as banned strings are out of scope of exclusion (C-006): they stay always-on blocking gates and never appear in excluded_surfaces.

Test-inventory groups (mission sonar-per-pr-coverage-reuse-01M2FR32, WP02): `unit` and `specify_cli_runtime` are rows for live test directories that had no declared home. Their roots are deliberately a SUBSET of globs other kept groups already own (never a new src/** claim), so adding them changes no path's group match and leaves the FR-004 fail-closed `unmatched` union semantics intact. Rationale and the rejected alternative are recorded in kitty-specs/sonar-per-pr-coverage-reuse-01M2FR32/traces/design-decisions.md.

CI-infrastructure group (spec-kitty#4386): `ci` is the first NON-src row in `groups`. It stays in `groups` (not non_src_router_groups) because the module registry consumes `groups` rows verbatim and tests/ci needs a registry row to gain per-PR execution via the ci-modules.yml matrix, which runs on every PR. Its roots claim CI-infrastructure paths (scripts/ci/**, .github/workflows/**) that no group owned before, so no path's existing match changes; being non-src it is excluded from the FR-004 `unmatched` union exactly like docs/corpus/e2e, by the same contract rule (router-two-authority.md Invariant 2), and no ci-router.yml job gates on it -- the per-PR executor is the module matrix, and a router tests (ci) job would double-run the suite per PR.

groups.note: spec-kitty#6336: src/kernel/activation_ledger_store.py (the activation ledger's kernel-side floor, ADR 2026-10-19-1) is claimed here as an OVERLAP root -- the `kernel` group still owns src/kernel/**. Its readers are tests/charter/activation/** and tests/charter/conformance/test_activation_ledger_conformance.py, which live in this module's test dirs, so a floor edit must select the charter shard (#6336's 2026-10-20 follow-up). Overlapping src ownership is the scrub's existing shape (core_misc/unit/execution_context each also own src/specify_cli/status/**). The activation STORE paths (.kittify/charter/*.yaml) and the internal-pack pin (packs/internal.source.yaml) deliberately do NOT join this group: they are non-src, and the router's `charter` filter must stay the verbatim transcription of this row, so they carry their own non-src router group (`charter_activation`, gate_selection.ACTIVATION_STORE_MODULE_FANOUT).

Minted as a module (issue #6125) so a dossier-source edit runs tests/dossier + tests/specify_cli/dossier per-PR instead of nightly-only. A mission-manifest edit reaches this module through the non-src router group mission_manifest (gate_selection.GROUP_MODULE_FANOUT), not a root here.

TEST-INVENTORY row (mission sonar-per-pr-coverage-reuse-01M2FR32, WP02/FR-006). This group exists to give a live test directory a declared home in the module registry so retiring the duplicate broad-measurement step does not remove its PER-CHANGE execution. It owns no src/** surface of its own: every root below is a VERBATIM copy of a glob another kept group already owns, so the router's path->group mapping and the FR-004 fail-closed `unmatched` union are unchanged (no path gains or loses a match). Roots/cov_targets are the subset of already-owned surfaces the directory's tests actually import -- never a surface no other group claims, which would silently narrow an unmapped src/** change away from the run-all catch-all. Covers tests/unit (already the first directory of the CLAUDE.md fast tier).

TEST-INVENTORY row (mission sonar-per-pr-coverage-reuse-01M2FR32, WP02/FR-006). This group exists to give a live test directory a declared home in the module registry so retiring the duplicate broad-measurement step does not remove its PER-CHANGE execution. It owns no src/** surface of its own: every root below is a VERBATIM copy of a glob another kept group already owns, so the router's path->group mapping and the FR-004 fail-closed `unmatched` union are unchanged (no path gains or loses a match). Roots/cov_targets are the subset of already-owned surfaces the directory's tests actually import -- never a surface no other group claims, which would silently narrow an unmapped src/** change away from the run-all catch-all. Covers tests/specify_cli/runtime (already the last directory of the CLAUDE.md fast tier).

CI-INFRASTRUCTURE row (spec-kitty#4386). The first NON-src group in `groups`: its roots are the CI-infrastructure paths (the CI scripts and the workflows that run them) whose regressions tests/ci guards, not product code, so it is deliberately NOT moved to non_src_router_groups -- it must stay in `groups` because the module registry consumes `groups` rows verbatim and tests/ci needs a registry row to gain per-PR execution (the module matrix runs on every PR). Mirrored 1:1 as the `ci` filter group in ci-router.yml. cov_targets follow the TEST-INVENTORY precedent: the src surfaces scripts/ci actually imports (kernel.clock in capture_shard_timings.py/select_source_artifacts.py, specify_cli.core.vcs.git in local_gate_parity.py) -- already owned by the `kernel` and `core_misc` groups, so no path's match set changes. Deliberate routing decision: CI-infra paths stay OUTSIDE the FR-004 fail-closed catch-all (that sensor is contractually unmapped src/** code, router-two-authority.md Invariants 1-2; these paths are not src and are now named) and no ci-router.yml job gates on the group -- the per-PR executor is the ci-modules.yml matrix shard, and a router tests (ci) job would double-run the suite per PR.

non_src_router_groups.note: Docs-only cheap lane; no src --cov subject.

Doctrine corpus + mission data leaves (#3008), plus the core-owned contracts/fixtures/ tree, which stays out of the wheel, the pins of the spec-kitty-events extras the reality check reads (#6915), and the kitty-ops/ Op data the reality check reads; non-src, no --cov subject.
End-to-end / cross-cutting suite, plus the first-run path, which an init change also routes here (#7741); not a src --cov subject.

Every Mission file plus every input that can change the mission-state audit verdict (#5864, #6058): the reducer dependency manifests, the audit-path CLI modules, the workflow and renderer; non-src, no --cov subject.

The doc-kitty docsite build inputs (#6930, ADR 2026-10-31-1 D-11): the pages, the site/ project, its folder contract, the built-site publication check and the link-gate wrapper (#6932), the legacy redirect map generator, its self-test and the moves ledger (#6933), the live-site probe the build runs on site/dist (#6938), the router workflow and the shared build definition it calls (#6937); gates only docs-site; non-src, no --cov subject.

#7870 (operator ruling 2026-11-25, option A): the orchestrator-api contract-shape module (tests/contract/test_orchestrator_api.py) carries no corpus mark, so both tests/contract router jobs (-m "corpus and not windows_ci") deselect it and no per-PR job ran it -- the class that blocked the RC9 cut (#7829/#7835/#7846). Gates only tests (orchestrator-api contract), which runs gate_selection.CONTRACT_SHAPE_PR_PATHS; the globs are what the module reads (the verb package incl. docstrings via inspect.getsource, the error classes it imports, the vendored contract its conftest loads, the contract layer every envelope passes through (core/contract_gate.py, missions/_read_path_resolver.py), the two prose surfaces whose error-code enumerations it parses, the module and conftest, and the test environment inputs (tests/conftest.py, pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, uv.lock; the contract_tools precedent). The package's other transitive imports are behaviour, covered by the execution_context shard's tests/specify_cli/orchestrator_api. NON-src on purpose, like path_literal_audit: every src path named is already mapped by a src-backed group, so this is an extra narrow lane, never a code-shard group. #7874 widens it to the other non-corpus tests/contract modules.

#6879: the runtime-home path-literal guard (tests/audit/test_no_legacy_path_literals.py, the #2171 limb) had no per-PR lane at all -- tests/audit is out_of_matrix_test_dirs and the only nightly lane naming it runs -m "fast or unit", which deselects the whole integration-marked module -- so a src/specify_cli/status/** diff ran no audit test, which is how #6367's literal reached main unseen (#6582). NON-src on purpose, like mission_state: the globs are **/-spelled so this stays an extra narrow lane gating one job, not a code-shard group (a src-backed group must also be a module-registry row, and claiming tests/audit as a module is a separate CI-budget decision -- issue candidate 2). It also must not narrow the FR-004 fail-closed sensor: every path it names is already mapped by a src-backed group, and src/specify_cli/paths/** -- the keystone resolver directory -- stays unmapped so a diff there still forces run-all, which runs this lane too. The deliberate over-match **/specify_cli/status/** also matches tests/specify_cli/status/**, so a status-test-only PR pays the same ~2 s of pytest (cost only, correctness unaffected; mirrors mission_state).

excluded_surfaces.note: Sync transport retired in The Convergence (#115). No filter group or --cov target may map to it.
Delivery subsystem retired with the sync transport.
Event-journal subsystem retired with the sync transport.
In-repo saas subsystem retired; SaaS is now an upstream client repo (saas_client is the live consumer, not this surface).
The websockets transport dependency was retired; excluded from every group and from the coverage denominator (E3 invariant).
